text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a burst of ECC/Xid messages on a subset of g4 nodes in us-west-2. Pods are getting kernel Xid and occasional GPU hangs. dmesg/journalctl captures are patchy. Can we agree on a tiny triage payload to collect immediately on first failure? :eyes:

ben: +1. We currently only grab the full journal during cordon/replace which is often too late. Proposal for minimal payload (aim <4MB gzipped): `dmesg -T --level=err,warn | tail -n 500`, `journalctl -k -b -n 1000`, `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 500`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `/var/log/nvidia-inst.log` if present, plus PCI info. Add node/k8s event UID metadata.

kai: How do we ship it? Signed S3 presigned URL or push to a central fast-blobstore? We need the file attached to the node event ID for quick lookup.

maria: Presigned S3 is fine. Collector should gzip and include node name + event UID in filename. Keep retention short (30d) and index to ES.

ben: Quick collector script we can drop in agent: ```#!/bin/bash
set -e
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
NODE=$(hostname)
EVENT=${1:-unknown}
OUT=/tmp/gpu-triage-$NOW.tar.gz
TMPDIR=/tmp/triage-$NOW
mkdir -p $TMPDIR
# kernel errors
(dmesg -T --level=err,warn | tail -n 500) > $TMPDIR/dmesg.txt
journalctl -k -b -n 1000 > $TMPDIR/journal-kernel.txt
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 500 > $TMPDIR/journal-nvidia.txt
nvidia-smi -q > $TMPDIR/nvidia-smi.txt
lspci -vvvnn | grep -i nvidia -A 20 > $TMPDIR/pci.txt || true
sha256sum $TMPDIR/* > $TMPDIR/checksums.txt
tar -czf $OUT -C /tmp triage-$NOW
# upload to presigned URL passed as $2
if [ -n "$2" ]; then
  curl -s --upload-file $OUT "$2" && echo "$OUT uploaded"
else
  echo "$OUT prepared"
fi
```

kai: Also capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output when possible. And include `lspci`/`ethtool` to check for PCI resets.

maria: Good call. Include `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` too; some of these are correlated with driver restarts.

node-watcher: drain initiated for node gpu-03a (us-west-2a) — detected repeated Xid 82 in kmsg. Pods being rescheduled.

ben: Parser idea: a lightweight Xid scanner that looks for Xid codes (13, 31, 79, 82) and tracks counts per node. Action matrix: if Xid 82 >=3 occurrences within 10m -> mark node flagged/flaky and schedule replace; if 13/31 -> escalate to hw-team and block auto-replace until manual review. Keep a TTL for flags (24h).

kai: We'll add a dedupe key derived from the sha256 of the tarball and event UID so we don't reupload duplicates. Also add a one-line JSON manifest in the tarball root with node, event, kernel, driver versions.

maria: Can someone draft a 1-paragraph oncall runbook? Steps we want: collect triage bundle, confirm Xid type, check `nvidia-smi -q` for ECC errors, look at last 200 dmesg lines, decide replace vs monitor. If replace: cordon and drain, attach trace to ticket. If monitor: annotate node and watch for recurrence. :shipit:

ben: I'll PR the collector + parser into the infra-agent repo and add the runbook snippet in the oncall doc. For now, run this against gpu-03a and paste `nvidia-smi -q` + last 100 dmesg lines here so hw-team can triage.

infra-bot: uploaded triage bundle to s3://redwood-gpu-traces/us-west-2/gpu-03a/2075123456-gpu-03a-triage.tar.gz :link:
